options.metric: Annual summed deaths by road-user category
options.denominator: None; raw annual death counts, not rates
options.grouping: Year (2013–2025) and road-user category (motorist or cyclist)
options.reason: Annual counts directly show the magnitude and year-to-year movement of deaths in each group.
options.answer: Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year from 2013 to 2025, ranging from 72 to 139 per year versus 10 to 31; cyclist deaths peaked at 31 in 2019 and 2023.
options.interpretation: This answers how the annual numbers of motorist and cyclist deaths compare: motorist counts were higher every year, with 72–139 motorist deaths and 10–31 cyclist deaths per year. Raw counts are a defensible direct comparison of the number of deaths, with no exposure denominator implied. It leaves unanswered the groups’ relative shares and any exposure-adjusted risk. It uses the 2013–2025 rows; rows outside those requested years (2012 and 2026) are filtered out, while among 2,132,218 in-range crash rows none are excluded for NULL required values (0.0%) and no included year is partial.

options.metric: Annual percentage share of combined motorist and cyclist deaths
options.denominator: Motorist deaths plus cyclist deaths in the same year
options.reason: Within-year shares emphasize the balance between the two categories while accounting for changes in their combined total.
options.answer: Cyclists made up 9.1%–27.4% of motorist-plus-cyclist deaths each year, peaking in 2019; motorists were the majority every year.
options.interpretation: This answers how motorist and cyclist deaths compare as a composition within each year: the cyclist share ranged from 9.1% in 2013 to 27.4% in 2019, and motorists were the majority each year. This denominator is defensible when the goal is to compare the relative balance rather than the absolute annual death total. It leaves unanswered the magnitude of the combined deaths and exposure-adjusted risk. It uses the 2013–2025 rows; rows outside those requested years (2012 and 2026) are filtered out, while among 2,132,218 in-range crash rows none are excluded for NULL required values (0.0%) and no included year is partial.
